fixes.explanation: Verse 2 says it plainly: the Spirit of God came upon Azariah son of Oded, so he went out to meet Asa, Judah's king. Out to meet Asa is exactly where he goes. And then he says, “Listen to me, Asa and all Judah and Benjamin.”
Praying in the temple sounds like a good plan, but it isn't what the text says. It says Azariah went out to meet Asa. When he speaks, he says, “Listen to me, Asa and all Judah and Benjamin.”

The hill country does show up in this passage, but later. Verse 8 mentions the cities Asa had captured in the hill country of Ephraim. In verse 2, though, Azariah goes out to meet Asa. Good guess, friend, but that's a different part of the story.

Verse 4 says, “But in their distress they turned to the LORD, the God of Israel, and sought Him, and He was found by them.” They turned to the LORD in their distress, and He was found by them. That's exactly what Azariah promised in verse 2.

Idols is right. Verse 8 says Asa “…removed the detestable idols from the whole land of Judah and Benjamin…” He also removed them from the cities he had captured in the hill country of Ephraim. Courage went straight to work.

The ark is a holy thing, but it doesn't come up in this passage. Verse 8 says, “He then restored the altar of the LORD that was in front of the portico of the LORD’s temple.” So the altar is what Asa restored.

Verse 9 says so: “…for great numbers had come over to him from Israel when they saw that the LORD his God was with him.” They saw that the LORD his God was with him, and they came. Verse 9 also says Asa assembled all Judah and Benjamin, along with those from the tribes of Ephraim, Manasseh, and Simeon who had settled among them.

Fasting and sackcloth aren't mentioned in this passage. Verse 12 says they entered into a covenant to seek the LORD, the God of their fathers, “…with all their heart and soul.” That's how they say they'll seek Him.

Verse 13 closes that door. It says whoever would not seek the LORD, the God of Israel, would be put to death, “…whether young or old, man or woman.” The text doesn't limit it to the men of Judah, so women are named right in the verse.

Right. Verse 13 says whoever would not seek the LORD, the God of Israel, would be put to death, “…whether young or old, man or woman.” The text doesn't limit it to the men. It's a heavy verse, but the wording is clear.
Weeping isn't mentioned in this passage. Verse 15 says all Judah rejoiced over the oath, for they had sworn it with all their heart. Rejoiced is the word the text gives.
A temple would be a big gift, but the text doesn't say He gave one here. Verse 15 says, “So the LORD gave them rest on every side.” Rest is what the text says He gave them.
Egypt doesn't come up in this passage. Verse 15 says, “So the LORD gave them rest on every side.” Rest on every side is the gift the text names.

Right. Asa did clear idols out, but verse 17 says, “The high places were not removed from Israel…” The text gives us both parts, the good work and what was left standing. So saying the high places were removed doesn't match the text.
Two paths? Not for Asa's heart, friend. Verse 17 says, “…Asa’s heart was fully devoted all his days.” That's the description the text gives, and divided isn't in it.

Proud? I get the guess, friend, but the text doesn't describe his heart that way. Verse 17 says, “…Asa’s heart was fully devoted all his days.” Devoted is the word it uses, and it says for how long: all his days.
Yes. Verse 19 says, “And there was no war until the thirty-fifth year of Asa’s reign.” Quiet right up until that year of his reign. That's a lot of peaceful batches.
The twentieth year isn't the one. Verse 19 says there was no war until the thirty-fifth year of Asa's reign. So the twentieth falls short of the number the text gives.
